# Project rules

## Comments

A comment says only what the code cannot. Never what the code does; a name or a smaller function says that. Call `pkg.Func()` when you need the parsed form.

- Strip narrating comments from any code you touch.
- **Do not** leave a commented-out block behind.
  It costs nothing to delete and git remembers it.
  - A doc comment on an exported identifier states what callers can rely on.
- Never

## Setup

```sh
- this bullet lives in a code fence and is not a rule
```

https://example.com/docs/setup

Every generated file in this repository is written by the build and a reviewer should never edit one by hand, because the next build would overwrite the change without warning, and the diff that follows would confuse everyone who reads the history of the file later on and nobody notices until much later in the week, by which time the person who made the change has forgotten what they were trying to do.
